title: SIEM Audit Export Beta — Customer Shortlist + Notes (working)
content:
Owner: Naomi (PM)
Program mgmt: Talia
Discovery / customer owners: Simran (SA), Colin (SE), Miguel (CSM), Liam (TAM)
Security review: Marcus / Kevin

Last updated: 2025-03-12

Purpose
- Working shortlist of candidate customers for the SIEM-ready audit export beta (hosted + dedicated only).
- Capture: customer SIEM stack, constraints (networking/residency), risk level, and a proposed plan (scope, success criteria, next steps).
- This doc is NOT customer-facing; keep candid notes.

Beta guardrails (must be explicit in all customer comms)
- Delivery semantics: at-least-once. Customers must deduplicate on event_id downstream.
- Supported sinks for beta: Splunk HEC, Datadog Logs intake, S3 delivery.
- Private/on-prem is NOT in scope for beta (can discuss follow-on roadmap).
- Backfill is limited (we need to confirm the default window; propose 7 days for beta unless Security/Compliance says otherwise).
- Filtering is available but v1 is “safe defaults” + allow/deny by category/action/resource; no arbitrary regex on payloads.
- Egress controls: destination validation + allowlist required for Splunk/Datadog endpoints.
- PII minimization: no raw prompts/completions; no request bodies; IP/user-agent only where applicable and policy-approved.

Selection criteria (what we’re optimizing for)
1) Representative destinations: 1–2 Splunk, 1 Datadog, 1 S3-only (or S3 + SIEM pull) 
2) Mix of compliance requirements: SOC2-only vs “higher bar” (HIPAA/financial)
3) Clear success criteria and engaged security ops contact (will validate in their SIEM)
4) Manageable volume for beta + willingness to tolerate rough edges / weekly check-ins
5) Networking/residency constraints we can support without one-off infra

Shortlist (top candidates)

Format key:
- Env: Hosted | Dedicated
- Destinations: Splunk HEC | Datadog Logs | S3
- Residency: US | EU | Mixed
- Networking: Public egress ok | Requires VPC/VPN | Allowlist-only | “No public internet”
- Risk: Low/Med/High (delivery risk + support risk + security risk)

1) Acme Banking ("Acme Bank")
- Stage: Security review / procurement influenced by SIEM export requirement
- Env: Dedicated (primary) + small Hosted sandbox
- Destinations requested: Splunk HEC (primary)
- SIEM stack: Splunk Enterprise + HEC; uses Splunk CIM-like mapping internally
- Residency: US-only
- Networking constraints: Strict egress allowlisting; prefers static outbound IP ranges; may ask for customer-managed VPC (out of scope for beta)
- Compliance drivers: SOC2 + internal bank security controls (audit trails, admin actions)
- Estimated volume: Unknown (needs confirmation). Initial guess: medium (admin actions + API key rotations, etc.)
- Filtering needs: Wants to filter out noisy “read-only” events; wants “auth/admin/security” categories always included
- Evidence asks (noted in call): delivery guarantees wording, retention vs export responsibility language, RBAC permissions list, encryption details
- Risks:
  - HIGH expectations (“bank-grade”) + low tolerance for missing/late events; may demand exactly-once language (we must hold the line)
  - Networking: if they require private connectivity, beta likely can’t satisfy
  - Support load risk: high (will open tickets quickly)
- Proposed beta fit: Conditional
  - OK if: they accept public Splunk HEC endpoint with allowlisted IPs + at-least-once + dedup
  - Not OK if: they require VPC private link / on-prem collector for beta
- Contact owners:
  - Redwood: Simran (SA), Colin (SE), Miguel (CSM)
  - Customer: (TBD — need named SecOps lead + Splunk admin)
- Next steps / open items:
  - Confirm: Can they provide a Splunk Cloud HEC endpoint reachable from public internet with allowlisting?
  - Ask for: HEC limits (events/sec), preferred index/source/sourcetype naming conventions
  - Provide: beta security FAQ + draft IAM/egress guidance

2) Helio Health
- Stage: Technical deep dive completed; likely willing beta design partner
- Env: Hosted first, Dedicated later (they’re evaluating both)
- Destinations requested: Datadog Logs (primary) + S3 archive (secondary)
- SIEM/observability stack: Datadog (security monitoring + log pipelines), S3 for retention / audits
- Residency: US
- Networking constraints: Generally flexible; will allow outbound to Datadog intake; needs clear docs for API key handling
- Estimated volume: Medium-high (they have many internal users + automated workflows). Need actual numbers.
- Filtering needs: Wants category-based allowlists (admin changes, API key operations, auth events) and resource scoping (workspace-level)
- Risks:
  - Medium: Datadog 403/permission pitfalls; key scoping is error-prone and will generate support churn
  - Medium: They may want more “enrichment” (tags, service names) than we have in v1 mapping
- Proposed beta fit: Yes (good Datadog anchor customer)
- Contact owners:
  - Redwood: Colin (SE), Liam (TAM), Miguel (CSM)
  - Customer: (TBD — need Datadog admin + security engineer)
- Next steps / open items:
  - Confirm Datadog site: US1 vs US3 etc (intake URL matters)
  - Confirm whether they require logs to be tagged by env/workspace; list required tags
  - Provide them a “test connection” flow plan + expected validation steps in Datadog

3) Quantiva
- Stage: POC scoping; strong residency requirements
- Env: Hosted (EU region) + potential Dedicated later
- Destinations requested: S3 delivery (primary); possible SIEM pull from S3 to their platform
- SIEM stack: “SIEM pulls from S3” pattern; may be Splunk or another internal system downstream
- Residency: EU-only (hard requirement)
- Networking constraints: Prefers no direct third-party SIEM endpoints; S3 in EU region; cross-account role required
- Estimated volume: Low-medium (but unknown). Their focus is evidence and completeness, not throughput.
- Filtering needs: Strict minimization; wants only security-relevant categories. Also requests deterministic schemas for compliance evidence.
- Risks:
  - Medium: EU-only requirements require careful region pinning (ensure exporter + storage are EU)
  - Low-medium: S3 adapter is the most controllable for us; fewer 3rd-party throttling issues
- Proposed beta fit: Yes (good S3/residency anchor)
- Contact owners:
  - Redwood: Simran (SA), Liam (TAM)
  - Customer: (TBD — need security/compliance owner + AWS owner)
- Next steps / open items:
  - Confirm EU AWS account + bucket policy expectations (SSE-S3 vs SSE-KMS)
  - Confirm cross-account assume-role preference and whether they require external ID
  - Clarify partitioning expectations (hourly vs daily) and file size preferences

4) Northstar Insurance
- Stage: Procurement/legal discussion; SIEM export is in security addendum
- Env: Dedicated (requested)
- Destinations requested: Splunk HEC (likely) OR S3 (fallback)
- Residency: US (likely) but they have some multi-region operations; confirm
- Networking constraints: Unknown; likely strict allowlisting + security reviews
- Estimated volume: Unknown
- Filtering needs: Probably wants “admin + auth + policy changes”; expects RBAC audit trail
- Risks:
  - Medium-high: legal/procurement timelines; they may treat beta as GA
  - Medium: support + escalations risk if they see it as contractual deliverable
- Proposed beta fit: Maybe (as a “late beta” if the product is stable)
- Contact owners:
  - Redwood: Miguel (CSM), Simran (SA)
  - Customer: (TBD)
- Next steps / open items:
  - Align with Legal on language: ensure no GA commitments, no private deployment promises
  - Confirm whether they can accept S3 delivery as interim if Splunk endpoint readiness is slow

Additional candidates (backup list)

5) Mid-market SaaS (name redacted in this working doc)
- Env: Hosted
- Destinations requested: Datadog only
- Pros: low process overhead; quick validation
- Cons: less representative of strict enterprise constraints
- Proposed beta fit: good “throughput + integration” sanity check if we need more signals

6) Existing enterprise customer asking via Support (see SUP-18422)
- Env: Dedicated
- Destinations requested: Splunk
- Pros: real pressure/use case; strong motivation
- Cons: comes in via ticket; may be escalatory; risk of “support-driven roadmap” during beta

Cohort proposal (3–5 accounts)
- Primary cohort (3): Helio Health (Datadog), Quantiva (S3 EU), Acme Bank (Splunk) — Acme only if networking constraints are workable
- Secondary/late cohort (1–2): Northstar Insurance + one mid-market Hosted account for fast feedback

Risk assessment rubric (quick)
- Delivery risk: downstream throttling (Splunk 429), Datadog key scoping / intake 403, S3 IAM/KMS misconfig
- Security risk: egress restrictions, secret handling expectations, PII policy compliance
- Program risk: procurement/legal expectations, “beta treated as GA”, slow customer-side SIEM admins

Current unknowns / open questions (need answers before final cohort selection)
1) Backfill window for beta: what do we commit to by default? (proposal: configurable up to 7 days; longer by exception)
2) Residency: Do we support EU-only end-to-end for the exporter + storage for the beta? If yes, what regions are allowed?
3) Networking: Do we have a clear statement for customers who want “no public egress”? (beta answer likely: not supported; offer S3-only as alternative if they can accept)
4) Splunk HEC: do we support Splunk Cloud + Enterprise equally? Any TLS/cert constraints? (customer-managed cert pinning is probably out)
5) Datadog: confirm supported sites (datadoghq.com, datadoghq.eu, etc.) and how we validate intake URLs under egress allowlist rules
6) Filtering model: finalize category taxonomy list we will publish (and what happens when categories change)
7) Event completeness: how do we message “at-least-once + lag during outage + eventual catch-up” for compliance without overstating guarantees?
8) “Who can configure exports”: need final RBAC role names & permissions to share with customers (Admin vs Auditor)
9) Support plan: who is on point for beta escalations (Slack channel + pager policy)? Define “beta support hours” if any.

Customer-side validation checklist (we should send in beta onboarding)
- Confirm destination reachable from Redwood egress (HEC URL / Datadog intake / S3 bucket + role)
- Set expected volume baseline
- Validate dedup strategy on event_id
- Confirm event fields mapping in SIEM (timestamp, actor, action, resource, workspace/tenant)
- Validate filtering behavior (allowlist/denylist) doesn’t drop required compliance events
- Confirm alerting rules (e.g., “new API key created”, “RBAC policy changed”, “export disabled”)

Notes from recent conversations (high-level, not exhaustive)
- Multiple customers expect “exactly-once”; we need consistent wording: at-least-once + idempotent event_id + customer dedup downstream.
- S3 delivery is the lowest operational risk and easiest to make compliant for residency; Splunk/Datadog have more external throttle/403 failure modes.
- Acme and Northstar will likely ask for Private/on-prem patterns; we should be prepared with a roadmap statement but not commit.

Action items
- Naomi: confirm beta cohort recommendation with stakeholders (Product/Security/SRE) by end of March.
- Simran/Colin: collect hard constraints for Acme + Helio (networking + destination details) and update this doc.
- Marcus/Kevin: confirm which audit event categories are “must include” for compliance baseline.
- Talia: draft onboarding runbook for internal enablement (feature flag allowlist + RBAC + destination test).

Changelog
- 2025-02-24: Initial draft created (Naomi)
- 2025-03-04: Added Acme / Helio / Quantiva sections; added cohort proposal
- 2025-03-12: Added Northstar notes + updated open questions
